requirement:
Awaiting the builder returns the decoded `R` that passes answer vetting under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.vet_answer`. The harness obtains the submitted value under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.submission.acceptance`.
rationale:
structural: The text of `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.judge.submission` has two clauses. The first says awaiting the builder returns the decoded `R` that passes answer vetting under `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.vet_answer`. The second says the harness obtains the submitted value under `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.submission.acceptance`. Both describe observable behavior, and both cite other requirements for the details. Neither prescribes a library, algorithm, signature, type, field, or delegation through a named interface. Any implementation that returns the vetted decoded value would satisfy the first clause, however the await is built. Any implementation that takes the value from the accepted submission would satisfy the second. That is true whether it uses one function or several. The `FnMut` callbacks, the ordering, and the `ValidationError::Graph` return are structural-looking details, but they belong to the cited `vet_answer` requirement. They are context here and are judged under that requirement. The same applies to the submission-count checks, which belong to `submission.acceptance`. There are no review roots and no implementation edges. No structural obligation here needs implementation evidence.

behavioral: The subject has one behavioral obligation: awaiting the `Ask` builder returns the decoded `R` that passes answer vetting. The cited requirements are context, so I checked that the tests apply them in this case. I did not reassess their own tests.

- **Scalar decode:** `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[default_tool_accepts_scalar_results_and_keeps_the_exact_prefix]` submits `{"result":true}` and asserts that awaiting `ask::<bool>()` returns `true`. It also checks that the `submit_result` schema types `result` as a boolean.
- **Structured decode:** `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[typed_submission_references_resolve]` submits `{"result":{"decision":"Yes"}}`. It asserts that the returned `Answer` has `Decision::Yes`. It also asserts the schema shape: only the `result` property, `additionalProperties` false, and `required` set to `["result"]`.
- **Returned value passes vetting:** `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[vetting_collects_corrections_and_rechecks_every_callback]` runs two submissions, `false` then `true`. The first is rejected by correction callbacks and the second passes every callback. The test asserts the await returns `true`, the later passing value. It asserts callbacks run on each submission (`seen == [false, true]`). It also checks that the correction feedback is returned and the conversation continues.
- **Vetting error ends the conversation (`vet_answer`):** `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[vetting_preserves_domain_errors_and_skips_later_callbacks]` asserts that a callback `Err` after an earlier correction request yields `ValidationError::Graph` with the original error. It also asserts that later callbacks are skipped and only one request is made.
- **Submission acceptance:** `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[assistant_text_and_provider_failure_cannot_become_typed_results]` shows that assistant text alone, even after a reminder, and provider failure never produce a typed result. `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[unknown_tools_return_errors_without_creating_inputs_or_preventing_submission]` shows that an unknown tool call does not block a later valid submission. `crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph/validation_tests.rs#fn[ending_without_a_corrected_submission_is_an_agent_error]` shows that ending without a valid corrected submission is an agent error. `crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph/validation_tests.rs#fn[explicit_insertions_preserve_order_repetition_and_selection_snapshots]` returns a decoded `Answer` through the builder.

Together these cover the success path (scalar and structured decode), the vetting interaction (only a vetted value is returned), and the failure paths (no result, or a vetting error, means no `R`). All the relevant tests carry a `{test}` reference to the subject. I found no unacknowledged gap.

text: :::{req} judge.submission
Awaiting the builder returns the decoded `R` that passes answer vetting under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.vet_answer`. The harness obtains the submitted value under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.submission.acceptance`.
:::{req} vet_answer
Each call to `Ask::vet_answer` appends an independent `FnMut` callback to this
request in either builder phase.
For each decoded submission, the harness invokes the callbacks in registration
order with the same `&R`, stopping at the first `Err`. Each callback retains
its state across submissions in the same conversation.
If any callback returns `Err(error)`, the harness MUST stop running callbacks
and end the conversation immediately, even if an earlier callback requested a
correction. Awaiting the `Ask` MUST return
`Err(ValidationError::Graph(error))` carrying the original `D::Error`.
:::{req} submission.acceptance
The harness checks the submission count in a complete model response before
checking submission arguments. An otherwise valid submission while any search
page is open returns a tool error listing every outstanding `search_id` and
instructing the agent to call `finish_search` before resubmitting. The request
stays open and retains its submission reminder. Once all delivered searches
are accounted for under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.behavior`,
exactly one `submit_result` call whose arguments are an object containing only
the `result` field supplies that field's value for decoding and vetting under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.vet_answer`. Acceptance ends the
conversation. Other tool calls in a response containing a submission are skipped.
Assistant prose remains conversation text.
